apiContracts: Chapter completion is exposed as a labeled progressbar with a bounded 0–100 value that updates during scrolling.
Novel chapter position remains separate from within-chapter completion.
The chapter drawer is connected to its trigger, moves focus when opened, and closes on Escape while restoring focus to the trigger.
Font-size controls expose descriptive accessible names.

migrationPlan.canonicalEntityReuse: No persistence changes; existing reading_positions remain unchanged.
migrationPlan.backwardCompatibility: No API or storage contract changes.
migrationPlan.rollbackOrForwardRepair: Code-only rollback; no database repair required.

uiLifecycle.clientBootBehavior: Reader progress and chapter drawer semantics are added after the existing reader route renders.

privacySecurity.csrf: Not applicable; no writes or routes added.

integration: Reader source and served bundle parity; accessible reader state and focus behavior assertions.

stagingSteps: Verify keyboard-only drawer open/close and focus restoration.
Verify progressbar value follows scroll and reports chapter completion only.

rollback.codeRollback: Revert the reader markup and focus/progress semantics together.

collisionReview.sharedSurfaceOwners: Reader and experience-shell own the browser behavior; platform-quality owns regression checks; architecture contract is updated.

changeSummary: Adds screen-reader progress semantics, accessible drawer relationships and focus management, Escape-to-close behavior, and descriptive font control names without changing reader persistence.
acceptanceCriteria: Progressbar exposes label, min, max and current chapter percentage.
Chapter completion is not confused with novel chapter position.
Drawer opens with focus moved to its close control and Escape closes it with focus restored.
No API, migration or production data changes.
